title: Local Work, Global Progress: A Convergence Theory of AI Agent Collaboration
abstract: arXiv:2610.28286v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Teams of large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly applied to complex tasks, but their collaboration protocols are mostly designed empirically, without convergence guarantees. We formalize collaborative problem solving as block optimization: each agent improves one part of a shared solution, guided by its local objective plus a correction for how its changes affect the other parts. A coordinator checks every proposal against the global objective and merges proposals that do not interfere with each other. We prove linear convergence up to an error floor that vanishes when the corrections are exact. Interfering proposals can also be merged once their combination has been checked; the rate then depends on how well the proposals actually combine, not on worst-case interactions. translated_title: 局部工作，全局进展：AI智能体协作的收敛理论
translated_abstract: 由大语言模型（LLM）智能体组成的团队正越来越多地被应用于复杂任务，但它们的协作协议大多是凭经验设计的，缺乏收敛性保证。我们将协作式问题求解形式化为块优化（block optimization）：每个智能体改进共享解的一部分，其指导依据是自身的局部目标，外加一个刻画其修改如何影响其他部分的修正项。一个协调者会依据全局目标检验每个提案，并合并互不干扰的提案。我们证明了线性收敛性，收敛至一个误差下限，当修正项精确时该误差下限会消失。对于相互干扰的提案，只要对其组合进行了检验，也可以进行合并；此时收敛速率取决于提案实际组合的效果，而非最坏情况的交互。在使用GPT-OSS-120B智能体的机器人路径规划任务中，三智能体团队在每次运行中都能找到无碰撞的规划方案，效果优于单一智能体控制所有……（原文此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文首次为LLM多智能体协作建立了收敛性理论：将协作求解形式化为块优化，每个智能体基于局部目标加修正项改进共享解的一部分，由协调者检验并合并提案，证明了可达到误差下限的线性收敛性，并在机器人路径规划任务中验证了多智能体团队总能找到无碰撞方案且优于单一智能体。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes the first convergence theory for LLM agent collaboration by formalizing it as block optimization—where each agent improves part of a shared solution guided by a local objective plus a correction term, and a coordinator checks and merges proposals—proving linear convergence up to a vanishing error floor, validated on robot routing where a three-agent team consistently finds collision-free plans superior to a single agent.
